notes: Hook order for PreToolUse matters: secrets and role-boundaries deny fastest/cheapest first; rd-freeze before red-before-green because a stale RD must block regardless of red-log state; detect-hazard is non-blocking (records only) and runs after the blocking guards so it never masks a deny; guard-state-transition only fires meaningfully on rd/*.md writes (no-ops elsewhere) — RDs are Markdown files with a YAML frontmatter block, not bare *.yaml (fixed 2026-07-28 after project-state.sh's rd/*.yaml glob was found to silently match zero real RDs).

guard-pipeline-order.sh (added 2026-07-29 per /cz:audit M4) only fires meaningfully on deliverables/*.md writes matching a named outer-pipeline artifact (SCOPE/SPEC/MODULEMAP/ARCH/WBS/EST/RISK/DELEGATION-MAP/DOR/DEVBOOK/RTM/WEEKLY/CASE-STUDY — plan §8.2's step table); it is a no-op on every other path, including rd/**, src/**, tests/**, and gate-records/** themselves, which the guards above it already own. Placed last because it never needs to preempt the others (a rejected write there never reaches a deliverables/*.md path anyway) and, unlike guard-state-transition (a single self-contained state-machine check), it reads gate-records/** written by the other guarded flows, so it makes sense to run once everything upstream of it in this same array has already had a chance to deny.
guard-claim-lock.sh is NOT wired here as a Write/Edit hook — it is invoked directly by /cz:rd and /cz:build at claim time, since a claim is a distinct action from a file write.

release-lock.sh (like restamp-lock.sh) is likewise NOT wired here — /cz:gate invokes it directly at step 8 when an RD is accepted, so the lock release is durably recorded (rd_release) in telemetry before the lock file is removed, added 2026-07-29 per /cz:audit UL-002.
Phase 3 risk (plan §13): if Claude Code hooks cannot intercept every write path, these guarantees become advisory. Fallback is /cz:audit retro-verification from git history + telemetry.

render-deliverable.sh is separate from the '*' PostToolUse block (and runs after it) because it only needs to fire on deliverables/**/*.md — it renders a sibling .html and rebuilds deliverables/index.html. It is purely cosmetic (human-readability) and must never deny a write; see docs/DELIVERABLES.md. Matcher changed from 'Write' to 'Write|Edit' (per /cz:health-check's Change-coupling finding: 32/120 rendered deliverables were stale because every DEVBOOK/understanding-log file gets touched by Edit far more often than by a full Write, and Edit never fired this hook) — the render itself is idempotent (re-renders the current on-disk content regardless of which tool produced it), so widening the matcher changes nothing about what gets rendered, only how often it stays current.

warn-rd-changelog.sh, warn-freshness.sh, warn-decision-coverage.sh (added per /cz:health-check's 2026-08-10 AIBOOTCAMP run) are all non-blocking (log + telemetry only, mirroring detect-hazard.sh's pattern — never cz_deny) and each closes one dimension health-check could previously only find after the fact: warn-rd-changelog flags a version>=2 RD with no notes: change-log (Change coupling); warn-freshness flags a src/**/tests/** citation of a just-superseded/withdrawn RD id, and separately flags a parent_req whose entire RD lineage just went dead (Freshness, Coverage); warn-decision-coverage flags a RISK.md hazard:HIGH module with no matching ADR-NNN section anywhere (Decision coverage). All three fire PostToolUse (after the write already landed) since they need to read the resulting on-disk state, not the incoming diff — see each script's own header for why a PreToolUse hard-block was rejected for these specific checks. They run in their own array (not folded into render-deliverable's) because warn-decision-coverage only fires on deliverables/RISK-*.md Write while the other two fire on rd/*.md Write|Edit — different matchers, so they cannot share one block with render-deliverable's deliverables/**/*.md scope.
